title: Geometry
description: A shape on the earth, held either by reference or inline.

@type.description: Always `Geometry` - a value type rather than an entity, like `Identifier` and `MonetaryAmount`. `schema:GeoShape` cannot do this job: its polygon is a space-delimited text string with no coordinate reference system, no multipolygon and no interior rings, and schema.org's own `GeospatialGeometry` is a declared placeholder that was never filled in. Exactly one of `contentUrl` or `coordinates` must be present.

geometryType.description: GeoJSON geometry type. MultiPolygon is the common case for real administrative areas, which have islands and exclaves.

contentUrl.description: URL of a GeoJSON resource. The default for anything shared, authoritative or large: a jurisdiction boundary is referenced by every record in that jurisdiction, and duplicating it into each is the drift SPEC section 1.2 exists to prevent.

coordinates.description: Inline GeoJSON coordinates. Permitted for geometry that is specific to one record and small - an alert polygon, a parcel outline - because real standards inline it and a profile that forbade it could not describe CAP. The validator warns above a vertex threshold rather than failing, since that is a publishing judgement rather than a correctness error.

sourceReferenceSystem.description: The CRS the publisher's authoritative source is held in, as an OGC CRS URI or 'epsg:NNNN' shorthand. This is provenance, not a claim about the coordinates here: GeoJSON mandates WGS84 longitude/latitude and forbids alternatives, so referenced and inline GeoJSON are always CRS84. Recording it matters because national-grid coordinates read as WGS84 land in the wrong hemisphere.

simplified.description: Whether this is a generalised rendering for display. A simplified boundary is not the legal boundary, and using one to decide whether an address falls inside a district gives wrong answers at the edges. A consumer needs to know which it has.

vertexCount.description: Approximate vertex count, where the publisher knows it.
